newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu goes on offensive over Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu goes on offensive over Jerusalem.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday ordered the closure of four Palestinian offices in Arab East Jerusalem in a move coinciding with a Washington visit by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
The decision was certain to draw Palestinian anger at a time of already high tensions over Israel's plan to build a new Jewish settlement in the eastern part of Jerusalem.

"Police will begin to act tomorrow and issue closure orders against four offices which beyond any legal doubt have been proven to be offices of the Palestinian Authority," Netanyahu's spokesman said in a statement.

Under Israel-PLO peace deals, the Palestinian Authority in charge of parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip cannot operate in Arab East Jerusalem, whose final status is to be decided in future peace talks.
The spokesman declined to name the offices and said Netanyahu ordered their closure on the recommendation of his adviser on terrorism, Meir Dagan.
In addition, Netanyahu instructed Police Minister Avigdor Kahalani to "remove by the end of the week Palestinian security men operating in Jerusalem", the statement said.
"The prime minister gave instructions to continue to examine if there are additional offices acting on behalf of the Palestinian Authority in Jerusalem," it said.

Netanyahu, under fire from Jewish settlers and other right-wingers over Israel's troop withdrawal from most of the West Bank town of Hebron in January, has repeatedly vowed to stand firm on Jerusalem.

Last year, the PLO closed two Palestinian offices in the east of the city after Israel demanded they be shut. The PLO said at the time it took the action to deprive Netanyahu of any excuse to slow peace moves.

Netanyahu's spokesman issued the statement only hours after Arafat said he still regarded the right-wing Israeli leader as a peace partner despite last week's decision to build 6,500 homes for Jews at Jabal Abu Ghneim, called Har Homa by Israel.
Netanyahu, speaking on Israeli Army Radio, said bulldozers would begin to move in two weeks on the pine-covered Jerusalem hill at the centre of an international controversy.
"From the standpoint of the survey work it's only a few days," the Israeli prime minister said. "We are determined to go on building in Jerusalem."

U.S. President Bill Clinton sided with Arafat at a White House meeting on Monday, saying Netanyahu's plan to build the homes in the city that will be subject to future Israel-PLO negotiation would fuel "mistrust".
Israel captured East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed it, a move not recognised internationally, to claim all the city as its capital.
The PLO sees construction at Jabal Abu Ghneim as an attempt to block its demand for East Jerusalem to become capital of a Palestinian state.
A U.N. Security Council debate scheduled to begin on Tuesday on the Israeli housing project was postponed until Wednesday at the request of the United States.

"We felt that a short delay would be helpful and we look forward tomorrow to a briefing by Chairman Arafat in the morning and then a discussion of the settlements issue in the afternoon," U.S. ambassador Bill Richardson said in New York.
At a Washington news conference on Tuesday, Arafat again bitterly denounced the Jerusalem building plan, calling it an illegal move that created a "real challenge" to the peace process.
Nevertheless, Arafat said: "It is our duty and our job and our target to carry on with the peace process...This is our strategic target."
Arafat said he considered Netanyahu his peace "partner" just as previous Labour prime ministers were.
Israeli moves in Jerusalem sparked violence in September. Sixty-one Arabs and 15 Israeli soldiers died in gun battles after Netanyahu opened a tourist tunnel entrance near Islamic shrines.
Netanyahu was due to meet Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Cairo on Wednesday, when he was likely to hear more criticism of the Jerusalem project.

The Israeli leader said he would convene a cabinet meeting this week to discuss carrying out the next withdrawal of Israeli troops from parts of the West Bank as agreed with the PLO in January. The redeployment is due to take place by Friday.
